about: Policy for h-uman's footprint: which build the published numbers describe, the hard budgets CI enforces, and when a fresh measurement should refresh the docs. Measurements live in footprint.json; scripts/footprint.py joins the two. Units: bytes, and SI megabytes (1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes) wherever a claim says MB.

builds.release-size: MinSizeRel + LTO, all channels, sqlite-vec OFF. The exact configuration of the release-size job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, so CI re-measures what the docs describe on every main push.
builds.release-preset: `cmake --preset release` (adds sqlite-vec, ML, embedded model, Cartesia, cron, feeds, update). What a user building the full release gets. Measured locally; CI does not build it.

binary_bytes.why: 2800 KB. Raised from 2600 KB after a linker-map audit of the 2611 KB binary found nothing to trim (__text 1809 KB, __cstring 512 KB, -Oz and no-unwind-tables already on); the growth was product code. Previously hard-coded in the release-size job (PR #424). Raise only with a measurement, never to make a red run green.

version_peak_rss_bytes.why: 8 MB, the long-standing 'Max Allowed' peak RSS of `human --version` in docs/standards/engineering/performance.md. It was never enforced anywhere until this file.

startup_ms_median.why: 100 ms, the long-standing 'Max Allowed' cold start in docs/standards/engineering/performance.md. Checked on the median of 20 warm runs, because a single sample on a shared CI runner is noise.

heal.why: A published '~N' or 'X.Y MB' value is refreshed when it is more than 5% away from a fresh measurement. That is a third of the 15% drift tolerance the binary-size claims were gated at before this file existed, so the docs refresh well before any claim is badly off. Bounds ('<9 MB') and ranges ('4-6 ms') refresh the moment a fresh measurement falls outside them. Nothing refreshes for noise inside those limits, which is what keeps the heal loop from opening a PR on every commit.
